findings.title: Embed template has invalid ERB and will not render
findings.body: `<%- end if %>` is not valid Ruby, so compiling `app/views/embed/best.html.erb` raises a SyntaxError. Any request that finds an existing topic and renders the best-comments iframe (the success path in EmbedController#best) fails instead of showing the discussion.

findings.title: Feed import crashes when an item has no content
findings.body: `i.content.scrub` assumes every SimpleRSS item has a non-nil `content` string. RSS items commonly only set `description` (and Atom items can omit content), and `String#scrub` does not exist on Ruby 2.0, which this app still boots. The first such item raises NoMethodError, aborts the whole hourly poll, and also aborts TopicRetriever when it calls `Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute` on an embed cache miss. There is no per-item rescue, so one bad entry blocks every later item.

findings.title: Imported HTML and embed URLs are stored and rendered unsanitized
findings.body: `TopicEmbed.import` appends the source URL into an HTML footer via string interpolation (`<a href='#{url}'>`) and saves the body with `cook_method: raw_html`. `Post#cook` then returns that raw string unchanged, and the embed view prints it with `raw post.cooked`. Feed items never pass through Readability or Sanitize, so script tags, event handlers, and `javascript:` URLs in RSS/Atom HTML are stored as the topic's cooked HTML and execute for every forum viewer, not just the iframe. The URL check only requires an `http(s)://` prefix, so a quote or `>` in the link/query breaks out of the footer anchor as well.

findings.title: open-uri fetch of attacker-influenced URLs enables SSRF
findings.body: `import_remote` does `open(url).read` with no redirect limit, timeout, or address filter, and `PollFeed` does the same for `feed_polling_url`. Embed misses enqueue `RetrieveTopic`, which calls this after only comparing `URI(embed_url).host` to `embeddable_host`. `open-uri` follows redirects, so a URL on the allowed host (or a feed entry whose link redirects) can make the app server request internal addresses such as link-local metadata endpoints. The embed referer check does not constrain where that URL ultimately connects.

findings.title: postMessage targetOrigin is a full referer URL, so resize never arrives
findings.body: `parent.postMessage(..., '<%= request.referer %>')` passes the parent page URL, including path and query. `postMessage` requires `*` or an origin (scheme, host, port only). Browsers reject a URL with a path, so the `discourse-resize` message is never delivered and the iframe in `embed.js` stays at its default height.

findings.title: Every embed cache miss re-imports the entire feed
findings.body: When `feed_polling_enabled` is on and the embed URL is not yet stored, `perform_retrieve` runs `Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute`, which downloads the feed and calls `TopicEmbed.import` for every item, synchronously inside the retrieve job. That work is already scheduled hourly, is not bounded by the 60-second per-URL Redis throttle once the job has started, and uses a blocking `open` with no timeout. A slow or large feed stalls Sidekiq and can be triggered repeatedly by embed traffic for URLs that are not in the feed.

findings.title: embed_url is limited to 255 characters
findings.body: `t.string :embed_url` uses the Rails default varchar(255), and `topic_id_for_embed` looks up the full URL exactly. Article and feed permalinks with long paths or tracking query strings will fail the insert (or be truncated, then never match the original `embed_url`). Those pages stay on the loading iframe and are re-fetched forever instead of embedding.

findings.title: Embed controller spec expects a call the controller does not make
findings.body: The success example stubs `TopicRetriever.new` and expects `retrieve`, but `EmbedController#best` only calls `Jobs.enqueue(:retrieve_topic, ...)`. As written the example fails, and nothing asserts that a job is enqueued, that `embed_url` is restricted to `embeddable_host`, or that the loading template is rendered. The poll-feed spec likewise never exercises `poll_feed` item parsing.
